lessons.title: ै (-ai) — the ai vowel sign
lessons.gloss: the ai vowel sign — the last of the four marks, and the one the word for money needs

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the section called Script until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Three chapters ago you learned ौ by adding a stroke to ो. The same trick works one more time.
ै (-ai) is ai, and it is े with a second stroke — the identical relationship ौ has to ो. Two marks, one rule, and with this one the four vowel signs of the e and o family are complete.
Hear them apart: के is ke; कै is kai, wider in the mouth. If you have met the pair ो / ौ, you already know what your voice has to do.
Copy कै twice with the model visible. Then write के beside it, and को and कौ underneath, and check that the second stroke falls in the same place in both pairs.
What is the difference between े and ै (-ai)? (One stroke.) Which other pair works the same way? (ो and ौ.)
Source: Devanagari ai vowel sign.

lessons.title: पैसे (paise) — money
lessons.gloss: money — a plural-only noun, and the first word this book has for the thing a price is paid in

segments.text: You can count to twenty and you cannot name the one thing people count most often.
पैसे — paise — money.

The word the sign in the last lesson was for. पैसे (paise) is Marathi's ordinary word for money, and it is plural only — there is no singular पैसा in this sense, the way English has no singular scissors. You will always hear it and always say it in this shape.
Underneath it is the paisa, the coin that is a hundredth of a rupee, which is why the plural is the natural form: money is counted in many small pieces.

Now the numbers earn their keep. किती पैसे (paise)? — how much money? — is the question the speaking paper's transactional part is built on, and you have owned किती since chapter thirty-seven with nothing to ask it about.

segments.instruction: mājhyākaḍe vīs paise āhet — I have twenty
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *mājhyākaḍe vīs paise āhet* — I have twenty]

segments.prompt: Ask how much money, then say you have twenty.
acceptedResponses: kitī paise? — mājhyākaḍe vīs paise āhet
किती पैसे? माझ्याकडे वीस पैसे आहेत

feedback.correct: A price asked and an amount held.
feedback.incorrect: kitī asks for the number; -kaDe plus aahe holds it.

segments.text: What shape is पैसे (paise) always in? (Plural.) Which sign did it need? (ै (-ai).)
Sources: Wiktionary: पैसे (paise).

lessons.title: रुपया (rupayā) — rupee
lessons.gloss: rupee — the unit a price is actually named in, and a word Sanskrit built out of shape

segments.text: पैसे (paise) is money in general. No price is ever quoted in it.
रुपया — rupayā — rupee.
वीस रुपये — vīs rupaye — twenty rupees.

This is the word a price is named in, and it is masculine, so it takes a plural ending after a number: one रुपया (rupayā), twenty रुपये. Say the pair out loud until the change is automatic, because a number is almost never said without it.

The history is a good one. Sanskrit रूप्य (rūpya) meant "wrought silver" — silver that had been given a SHAPE, from रूप (rūpa), form. A rupee is, at root, shaped metal. The same coin name travelled out of India far enough that it is now the currency of half a dozen countries.
With a number in front of it you can finally answer the transactional part of the speaking paper: किती? — वीस रुपये.

segments.instruction: rupayā, then vīs rupaye — and hear the ending change
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *rupayā*, then *vīs rupaye* — and hear the ending change]

segments.instruction: say इ and name a word it opens
segments.source: [YOU RECALL: say **इ** and name a word it opens]

segments.prompt: Ask how much, then answer twenty rupees.

feedback.incorrect: rupayaa becomes rupaye after a number.

segments.text: What did रूप्य mean in Sanskrit? (Wrought silver — shaped metal.) What happens to रुपया (rupayā) after a number? (It becomes रुपये.)
Sources: Wiktionary: रुपया (rupayā).

lessons.title: A price asked and answered
lessons.gloss: a price asked and answered — the first transaction this book can carry out

segments.text: Twenty numbers, a word for money and a word for the currency. That is a whole exchange, and it is the first one.

segments.instruction: kitī rupaye? — and answer with any number to twenty
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *kitī rupaye?* — and answer with any number to twenty]

segments.instruction: mājhyākaḍe paise āhet — I have money
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *mājhyākaḍe paise āhet* — I have money]
